purpose: Pinned GraphQL corpora for the GRAPHQL analyzer lane. Every record names an exact revision so a measurement can be re-run and get the same bytes. A corpus without a revision is an anecdote — this file exists because the m12 GraphQL corpus layer was unreproducible when this work started: validation/m12/results/graphql-*.json pinned /home/ishaq2321/bb_tests/repositories/graphql-js, which no longer existed, so every script under script/m12/graphql-*.ts CRASHED on `git rev-parse` while their artifacts sat on disk claiming `passed: true`.

reestablished.how: the corpus is re-established here with revisions, and the m12 scripts now read a path that exists; script/m12/graphql-node-types-compare.ts and the two corpus scripts take the corpus as an ARGUMENT rather than a hard-coded default, so a corpus is a choice of the invocation instead of a constant that can rot silently

corpora.name: graphql-js
corpora.whyThisOne: The GraphQL specification's own reference implementation, and the only repository in this set that ships the REAL GitHub public schema (benchmark/github-schema.graphql, 20,367 lines, 3,242 symbols) — the single largest real-world GraphQL SDL document bb can be measured against. It also ships benchmark/kitchen-sink.graphql, the specification's own torture test, which is deliberately invalid in places and therefore doubles as the lane's negative control.

knownNegativeFixture.measured: 0 grammar error nodes under the wired grammar, because the two constructs it used to break — a directive on a variable definition and an escaped triple-quote inside a block string — are fixed in the vendored grammar
knownNegativeFixture.verdict: NO LONGER A NEGATIVE CONTROL, and the artifact no longer claims it is. It was listed as a grammar limitation until this work; keeping a fixed defect in a table of known limitations is worse than an empty table, because the artifact would claim a limitation a reader can no longer reproduce. The 113-construct battery is what guards grammar regressions now.

corpora.name: graphiql
corpora.whyThisOne: The reference IMPLEMENTATION's test corpus, and the densest source of the constructs a production GraphQL tool meets: `... on X` inline fragments, fragment spreads, aliases, nested selection sets, multi-interface objects, block descriptions, described arguments, described enum values, `extend type`, and — in `graphql-toolkit/.../sorareSchema.graphql` (1,809 symbols) and `graphql-language-service/benchmark/fixtures/github.graphql` (3,228 symbols) — two more very large real schemas. Two files here are the lane's `interface X implements Y` and `repeatable` regression controls.
corpora.whyItMatteredMost: it is where the previous grammar's phantoms were measured: `packages/vscode-graphql-syntax/tests/__fixtures__/descriptions-and-values.graphql` lost a whole fragment definition to an ERROR region and published a phantom anonymous operation in its place

corpora.name: neo4j-graphql
corpora.whyThisOne: An Apollo FEDERATION subgraph, which is the dialect where a schema's meaning lives in its directive APPLICATIONS: @key, @external, @requires, @override, @link. Its `packages/apollo-federation-subgraph-compatibility/schema.graphql` is the single most productive file in the corpus for the previous-grammar phantom measurement — a described `extend type User` became an ERROR and the analyzer published four invented references (`anonymous_operation_1566 -> Int`, `-> ID`, `-> @external`, `-> @requires`) while losing five real field symbols.

repositoriesExaminedAndNotCloned.note: recorded so the choice is auditable. Each was checked for tracked .graphql/.graphqls/.gql paths with `git clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout` and `git ls-tree -r HEAD --name-only`, which downloads no blobs. graphql-js ships exactly 2 such files, which is why this set is three repositories and not one.

previousGrammar.why: the bytes this lane replaced, kept so the extraction A/B (12 -> 4 error files, 20 -> 7 error nodes, +4 symbols, +76 relationships) is reproducible forever rather than being a one-time observation. The upstream SOURCE it was built from is not recoverable — it predates optional($.description) on schema_definition and optional($.directives) on variable_definition, and the GitHub API surfaces no tag for that commit — which is recorded as a rejected alternative in the grammar pin's decision.
